notebooks.title: Rational Agency and Process Continuity
notebooks.summary: This research synthesizes the tension between rational agency as a normative ideal and the adaptive, budget-controlled strategies necessary for practical process continuity in autonomous systems. By integrating insights from optimal growth theory and verifiable autonomous systems, this notebook clarifies why adaptive, redundant paths are functionally more stable than strict, singular optimal paths.
notebooks.findings:
Rational agency serves as an ideal behavioral norm, but strictly optimal paths are inherently unstable in complex, real-world decision environments. [source-c1886e4dad8a40a0]

Rational agent frameworks can provide actionable assurance for machine-driven decision-making. [source-237bc591d86a41a7]
notebooks.limitations: The integration relies on macro-level economic analogies and assumes potential for verifiable agency; empirical data on micro-agent longitudinal preference persistence is currently sparse.
notebooks.next_questions: To what extent can adaptive, budget-controlled heuristics be formally verified in high-stakes autonomous decision-making?
notebooks.reason: Revision required to integrate new evidence on rational agency assurance, deepening the understanding of decision-making continuity.

notebooks.title: Path Dependence in Multi-Agent Interaction Protocols
notebooks.summary: This synthesis evaluates how initial communication constraints in MARL systems function as structural precursors, guiding the trajectory of emergent social dynamics. By projecting existing communicative MARL (Comm-MADRL) approaches into a multidimensional space, this research highlights that interaction protocols are not merely operational settings but critical determinants of long-term preference stability.
notebooks.findings: Initial communication constraints in multi-agent environments serve as foundational structural precursors for emergent agent social dynamics. [source-07300ea4ef074c4f]
notebooks.limitations: Evidence primarily reflects structural classification of MARL architectures; lacks long-term longitudinal data on agent preference persistence during non-stationary training.
notebooks.next_questions: Do specific communication constraints create 'basins of attraction' for agent preference formation that are resistant to later environment changes?

notebooks.title: Formalizing Value System Learning from Demonstrations
notebooks.summary: This notebook explores the integration of demonstration-based value learning within MARL frameworks. It finds that leveraging communicative architectural constraints offers a viable mechanism for enforcing alignment constraints, while game-theoretic perspectives provide a necessary formal background for objective definition.
notebooks.findings: Integrating game-theoretic and machine learning perspectives provides a rigorous foundation for formalizing agent objectives in MARL. [source-4836c72e1aac41b3]
notebooks.limitations: Integration with minimax game frameworks for RLHF is hypothesized; requires further empirical testing on complex agent-demonstrator interaction tasks.
notebooks.next_questions: Can minimax game formulations uniquely identify latent human values from demonstrations without over-fitting to noise?

We continue to prioritize the rigorous evaluation of how stochastic early interactions constrain long-term agent behaviors, maintaining our commitment to identifying non-stationary training effects despite current search limitations.

detail.title: Rational Agency and Process Continuity
detail.summary: This research synthesizes the tension between rational agency as a normative ideal and the adaptive, budget-controlled strategies necessary for practical process continuity in autonomous systems. By integrating insights from optimal growth theory and verifiable autonomous systems, this notebook clarifies why adaptive, redundant paths are functionally more stable than strict, singular optimal paths.
detail.findings:
Rational agency serves as an ideal behavioral norm, but strictly optimal paths are inherently unstable in complex, real-world decision environments. [source-c1886e4dad8a40a0]

Rational agent frameworks can provide actionable assurance for machine-driven decision-making. [source-237bc591d86a41a7]
detail.limitations: The integration relies on macro-level economic analogies and assumes potential for verifiable agency; empirical data on micro-agent longitudinal preference persistence is currently sparse.
detail.next_questions: To what extent can adaptive, budget-controlled heuristics be formally verified in high-stakes autonomous decision-making?
detail.reason: Revision required to integrate new evidence on rational agency assurance, deepening the understanding of decision-making continuity.
